controls.title: Logical access security software, infrastructure, and architectures
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the access-control policies enforcing those events are well-designed, that the right principals had the right entitlements, or that the system architecture itself satisfies the criterion. The chain is the audit log; it does not substitute for the access-control system being audited.
controls.what_we_prove: Every logical-access event affecting in-scope systems is hash-linked, signed under a customer-bound key, and timestamp-anchored. The resulting chain is tamper-evident: any after-the-fact insertion, deletion, or reordering is mathematically detectable.

controls.title: Logical access security measures restrict access to information assets
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the enforcement decisions themselves were correct. The chain records what the system decided, not whether the decision matched policy.
controls.what_we_prove: Enforcement decisions (allow/deny) recorded by in-scope systems are present in the chain in the order they occurred, with cryptographic anchoring that proves no decision was retroactively edited or omitted.

controls.title: Restrict transmission, movement, and removal of information
controls.what_we_dont_prove: Whether transmissions were authorized, whether their destinations were appropriate, or whether the data being moved was the data that should have been moved. The chain is evidence of recording, not of correctness.
controls.what_we_prove: Data-movement and data-egress events emitted by in-scope systems are recorded with stable cryptographic ordering and signed timestamps. An auditor can confirm what was transmitted, when, and that the log has not been edited since.

controls.title: Detect anomalies via monitoring of system components and operations
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the monitoring infrastructure detected the right things, that the detection thresholds were appropriate, or that nothing was missed. The chain is silent about events that were never emitted to it.
controls.what_we_prove: Anomaly-detection events surfaced by the customer's monitoring infrastructure and submitted to Aleutian are stored with tamper-evident ordering. An auditor can reconstruct the exact sequence and timing of what was detected.

controls.title: Detect security events and understand their nature
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the events were correctly classified as security events, that the response was timely, or that the right people were notified. Those are downstream of detection.
controls.what_we_prove: Security events submitted to the chain carry signed timestamps and stable ordering, so an auditor can establish what was detected and in what sequence. The chain is admissible evidence of the detection event itself.

controls.title: Respond to identified security incidents
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the response was appropriate, complete, or timely. The chain records what was done; whether what was done was the right thing is the auditor's call.
controls.what_we_prove: Incident-response actions logged to the chain (assignment, status changes, remediation events, closeout) are stored with tamper-evident ordering. An auditor can reconstruct the exact response sequence and verify no step was later edited.

controls_out_of_scope.reason: control environment (board oversight, integrity, ethics) is organizational, not chain-evidenced
communication and information practices are process-level, not chain-evidenced
risk assessment is a process, not a logged event
monitoring meta-controls; CC7.x covers the concrete chain-evidenced overlap
control activities are process design, not chain-evidenced
access onboarding is an HR process, not a chain-logged event
periodic access reviews are a process, not chain-evidenced
physical access controls are out of scope for a cryptographic audit chain
physical media disposal is out of scope for a cryptographic audit chain
change management is a process; specific changes may be logged elsewhere but the management of change is not chain-evidenced
risk mitigation activities are process-level, not chain-evidenced
availability evidence (uptime, RTO/RPO attainment) is not surfaced by an event chain
confidentiality classification policy is not chain-evidenced; access events to classified data are covered under CC6.x
processing integrity is application-correctness, not chain-evidenced
privacy series is heavily process-driven; specific privacy-event logging may be covered in framework-specific seeds (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA)
